Integration planning – draft workstream overview (v0.3)

The integration office will be organised around six workstreams: finance, HR, IT, procurement, legal/compliance and communications. Each workstream lead will report weekly to the integration steering committee, which will be chaired by the COO and will meet every Tuesday from signing until at least six months after completion. The finance workstream will focus on aligning the chart of accounts, moving the acquired business onto group treasury and harmonising month-end close timetables; experience from previous integrations suggests this takes two to three quarters. HR will need to map job grades, review bonus schemes and prepare consultation materials where local law requires them, noting that the works council at the Marlow Filtration plant in Bremen must be consulted before any change to shift patterns is announced. IT will run a separate discovery on the ERP landscape, since early indications are that the business still runs a heavily customised legacy system that will not be migrated in year one. Procurement will look for quick wins on shared suppliers, especially steel and freight. Legal/compliance will own the contract novation tracker, the sanctions screening refresh and the policy roll-out. Communications will prepare the day-one pack for employees, customers and suppliers. Please send comments on this structure to the integration office by Friday so the charter can be finalised.

Please proofread this section of the board paper, don't change the numbers:

3. Transaction overview

Project Driftwood is the proposed acquisition by Harrowgate Industries of the entire issued share capital of Kestrin Automation Ltd, a privately held designer of motion-control systems headquartered in the Midlands. Kestrin has approximately 340 employees and generated revenue of £61m in the last financial year. The proposed consideration is £94.5 million on a cash-free, debt-free basis, of which £12 million will be retained in escrow for 18 months as security for warranty claims. An additional earn-out of up to £15 million is payable if Kestrin achieves agreed EBITDA targets in FY27 and FY28.

4. Precedents

The structure mirrors our 2023 acquisition of Fellbeck Tooling, which was publicly announced and completed within four months. As with Fellbeck, we propose a locked-box mechanism.

5. Advisers and costs

External legal fees for Project Driftwood are estimated at £850k, in line with the budget approved in July.

6. Recommendation

The Board is asked to approve Project Driftwood on the terms set out above and to delegate authority to the CEO and CFO to agree the final transaction documents.
note: Repeated codename and target. Not deal terms: the target's revenue (£61m), adviser fees (£850k), and the public Fellbeck precedent.
